classification.difficultyReason: The overlap requires two cases depending on whether the ace of hearts is selected.

content.prompt: How many ways can you deal a hand of five cards from a standard deck so that the hand contains exactly one ace or exactly one heart?

answer.short:
$1\,531\,638$ ways.

Use inclusion–exclusion, splitting the overlap according to whether the ace of hearts is included.
answer.worked:
Let $A$ be the set of hands containing exactly one ace and $B$ the set containing exactly one heart.

$$\begin{align*}|A|&=\binom{4}{1}\binom{48}{4}\\|A|&=778\,320\\|B|&=\binom{13}{1}\binom{39}{4}\\|B|&=1\,069\,263\end{align*}$$

For a hand in both sets, either it contains the ace of hearts and four cards that are neither aces nor hearts, or it contains one of the three other aces, one of the twelve other hearts and three cards that are neither aces nor hearts. There are $36$ cards that are neither aces nor hearts.

$$\begin{align*}|A\cap B|&=\binom{36}{4}+3\times12\binom{36}{3}\\|A\cap B|&=315\,945\\|A\cup B|&=|A|+|B|-|A\cap B|\\|A\cup B|&=778\,320+1\,069\,263-315\,945\\|A\cup B|&=1\,531\,638\end{align*}$$
